source: Van Andel, T.H. (1975): Mesozoic/Cenozoic calcite compensation depth and the global distribution of calcareous sediments. Earth and Planetary Science Letters, 26, 187-194.
figure_provenance: Digitized from a reproduction of Van Andel's three-basin CCD curves supplied by the user in-conversation (2026-09-08), annotated with present-day asterisks after Broecker, W.S. & Clark, E. (2007) marking the early-Holocene carbonate preservation event depth. The reproducing paper itself was not identified -- if you know which one it is, tell me and I'll correct this citation.
method: HAND-DIGITIZED BY EYE from a rendered chart image, not pixel-traced (no source image file was available on disk for programmatic digitization). Treat as coarser than a WebPlotDigitizer-style extraction: age values are approximate to roughly +/-3 Ma, depth values to roughly +/-0.15-0.2 km, especially at inflection points. Re-digitize from the original PDF figure if higher fidelity is ever needed.
present_day_asterisk_note: Each panel carries a present-day (~0 Ma) asterisk from Broecker & Clark (2007), offset from Van Andel's own t=0 curve value -- per the original caption, today's CCD is interpreted as ~0.75 +/- 0.40 km shallower than the asterisk position (an 11+/-5 umol/kg CO3-- decline since the early-Holocene preservation-event peak the asterisk marks). Not applied here; carried as a separate field per basin for a later prep step to decide how to use.

atlantic_south.note: Eastern-basin asterisk per the original caption.

atlantic_north.note: Same asterisk as atlantic_south -- one present-day marker shared by both Atlantic curves in the figure.
